Packed signs that do not come back: a deployment audit of LittleBit

The shipped unpacker in SamsungLabs/LittleBit (commit {{upstream_commit_short}}) reads a -1 sign back correctly only at bit 0 of each 32-bit word. This page shows the recorded evidence, the one-line fix, how storage should be counted, and a tiny real-model pilot whose quality result is negative.

Scope, read first

  • Sections 1 to 4 are component level. Section 5 is a tiny wiring pilot: {{pilot.model}}, {{pilot.steps}} QAT steps on {{pilot.input_tokens}} input tokens, scored on {{pilot.scored_tokens}} held-out tokens, one seed, one run, {{pilot.device}} {{pilot.dtype}}. It is not a benchmark and not a replication of any published LittleBit result.
  • No new experiment was run for this page. Every number is read from files recorded at release {{data_release}} and listed with their SHA-256 under Provenance.
  • Not affiliated with or endorsed by the LittleBit authors or Samsung. No novelty claim.

1

The shipped unpacker drops most -1 signs

The packer stores one sign per bit, least significant bit first: column j of a row is bit j % 32 of word j // 32, and a set bit means -1. The upstream unpacker then reads bit k with a left shift:

{{patch.removed}}

Only bit 0 of the shifted value is inspected, and a left shift by any k >= 1 clears bit 0. So a -1 survives only at in-word position 0. Through the actual upstream functions, {{unpack.cases}} recorded cases ({{unpack.byte_tiled}} byte-tiled rows, {{unpack.one_hot}} one-hot rows and {{unpack.sign_example}} fixed patterns, at widths 1, 7, 8, 31, 32, 33 and 64) decode exactly in {{unpack.exact}} cases; {{unpack.errors}} signs come back wrong, every one of them a -1 read as +1. A corrected decoder recovers {{unpack.corrected_exact}} of {{unpack.cases}} from the same packed words, so the packer is correct.

{{table.widths}}

2

A one-line fix

Replacing the left shift with a right shift reads every bit. The proposed patch changes two characters on one line:

- {{patch.removed}}
+ {{patch.added}}

Applied in memory to the unmodified upstream source, the patched unpacker decoded {{patch.patched_exact}} of {{patch.cases}} recorded cases exactly, against {{patch.unpatched_exact}} of {{patch.cases}} without it. The upstream checkout was not modified, the patch has not been sent upstream, and the official full-model loader was not run; full-model reloads were emulated.

3

What gets packed: the dual-path binary low-rank layer

Each converted linear layer in upstream LittleBitLinear computes, for input x:

{{formula}}

{{formula_note}}. Uq and Vq are the binarized factors whose signs are packed into 32-bit words when a checkpoint is saved; u1, u2, v1 and v2 are scale vectors. The defect in section 1 corrupts Uq, Vq and their residual counterparts on reload.

4

Storage: disk bytes and resident bytes, kept apart

Disk and memory use different data types, so they are reported in separate panels and never summed or compared across. Tokenizer and config files ({{excluded.bytes}} bytes) are excluded from every weight count. The KV cache is not a weight: for {{kv.tokens}} tokens in FP32 it is {{kv.bytes}} bytes for both models, unchanged by LittleBit.

5

Tiny real-model pilot: a negative result

All {{pilot.modules}} linear layers in the transformer blocks of {{pilot.model}} were converted to upstream LittleBitLinear (eff_bit {{pilot.eff_bit}}, residual path, ITQ {{pilot.itq}}, seed {{pilot.seed}}), trained for {{pilot.steps}} QAT steps on {{pilot.input_tokens}} input tokens on {{pilot.device}} in {{pilot.dtype}}, saved packed, reloaded with a corrected decoder and scored on {{pilot.windows}} held-out windows ({{pilot.scored_tokens}} tokens). Perplexity stayed about {{ratio.qat}} times the original. Section 5 is a wiring check of the harness, not evidence about LittleBit at its published settings.

6

What this does not show

  • No statement about the LittleBit papers or their reported results. The pilot model, budget, precision and hardware all differ from the published settings, and {{pilot.model}} is outside the papers' model table.
  • No statistics: one seed, one run, {{pilot.windows}} contiguous windows. No validated 4-bit baseline, no smaller same-family model, no task accuracy, no end-to-end latency or throughput.
  • The official full-model loader quant_util.load_quantized_model was not run; reloads emulate its packed path. Reload identity was checked on one 128-token validation window per checkpoint.
  • The 3D diagram is structural. Its sizes and sign tiles are placeholders and carry no measurement.
